description: Cursor-based pagination API returns duplicate records across pages due to an off-by-one slicing error when seeking past the decoded cursor identifier.
spec_notes: Invariant: Slicing after a cursor item must strictly start at index + 1, and return next_cursor as None on the final page.

tests.test_paginator.py:
from models import Item
from paginator import Paginator

def test_first_page_no_cursor():
    items = [Item(f"id_{i}", f"Item {i}") for i in range(10)]
    paginator = Paginator(items)
    res = paginator.query_page(limit=3)
    assert len(res.items) == 3
    assert res.items[0].id == "id_0"
    assert res.items[2].id == "id_2"
    assert res.next_cursor is not None

def test_subsequent_page_no_duplicates():
    items = [Item(f"id_{i}", f"Item {i}") for i in range(6)]
    paginator = Paginator(items)
    
    page1 = paginator.query_page(limit=2)
    assert [it.id for it in page1.items] == ["id_0", "id_1"]
    assert page1.next_cursor is not None
    
    page2 = paginator.query_page(limit=2, cursor=page1.next_cursor)
    # Must be id_2 and id_3, not id_1 duplicated
    assert [it.id for it in page2.items] == ["id_2", "id_3"]
    
    page3 = paginator.query_page(limit=2, cursor=page2.next_cursor)
    assert [it.id for it in page3.items] == ["id_4", "id_5"]
    assert page3.next_cursor is None # Reached end
